body: It would be great, but this is unlikely to change. Changing it could/would cause existing applications to misbehave. I'd rather not break code twice (once for this and then again in 3.0)

@bar: Yes, definitively. Same behaviour with `belongsTo`.

@markstory: But currently it makes `afterFind` nearly impossible to use. Of course, it would break existing applications, but in a next version, I think it is right to break backwards compatibility. For sure not the first time, that CakePHP changes some behaviour in a positive way :-)
@janriokrause You can specify limit in association config too, so perhaps re binding the association with limit might prevent the issue you are having.

@janriokrause Actually:
- `hasOne`
- `belongsTo`
- `hasMany` with `limit` set
- `hasMany` with no `foreignKey` set (but with `conditions`)

are processed by the [same code](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/2.5/lib/Cake/Model/Datasource/DboSource.php#L1371-L1373). It is related to #2268, which does not surprise me by now :p

@markstory I believe every developer dealing with `afterFind()` operations ends up using the [infamous tests](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14106283/cakephp-2-x-is-the-primary-flag-on-modelafterfind-actually-useful?answertab=votes#tab-top) because of this, so I believe fixing it will not break (buggy) BC.

The hasMany cases should all be the same - regardless of limit or other settings.
Same for hasOne and belongsTo which belong together (and only those two).

What if we correct it in 2.5 and state in the migration guide what to modify/check for in the callbacks/code after migrating the core? Too many occurrences and changes also for controllers and views probably?

@dereuromark I'm on the verge of fixing this, the double bug #2268 and other related issues, but every time I encounter some solution I can`t change the actual API and it sucks.

The most easiest way to achieve is (not surprisingly) to use the same format when dealing with `afterFind()` (and `DboSource::_filterResults()` actually).
Because the code is undocumented, I'm quite new to it, and it's a beast on its own :) I'm having a very _nice_ time (learning a lot) while I characterize it and decouple it.

> I think it is right to break backwards compatibility. For sure not the first time, that CakePHP changes some behaviour in a positive way

Breaking compatibility generally only happens in major releases eg. (2.x.y). Doing it mid-cycle in 2.x makes upgrading harder, and makes our promises of API/feature compatibility moot.

My code is full of the dirty tests (mentioned by @bar ) to make afterFind() callbacks really usable.

Read the [afterFind() document](http://book.cakephp.org/2.0/en/models/callback-methods.html#afterfind) and there is a line saying:

```
If a model is queried as an association the format of $results can differ; instead of the result you would normally get from a find operation, you may get this...
```

The words "can differ" and "may get" really suck. I think nearly all people using this callback deal with this in two ways:
1. Assume the `$results` is always in the first format in the document, and simply ignore the second possibility since it is rarer.
2. Try to determine the format by `$primary` argument first and soon to fail. Then do some crazy google and find the infamous tests. Use the dirty test unwillingly like I do.

Thus unifying the format into the first case in the document will probably work fine for most people. A notice in the migration guide will help the rest.

I think it is OK to make such change in 2.4 -> 2.5 upgrade. However the decision is up to you guys. Just hope not to come across such problems in 3.0 :)

There's no question the different possible array format are beyond crazy. But backwards compatibility is pretty important. People having been living with this craziness all these years and they can live with it in 2.5 too :)

All these problems will be gone in 3.0 which has a shiny new ORM (which is getting close to be ready) without all these wacky "features".

I suddenly come up with a question for this **BC** problem: can anyone tell me what the _old behavior_ really is or should be?

There is no single piece of document telling users when the callback result set is in the first format and when is in the second. Nor is any reliable way to determine it in the code (even undocumented ways, AFAIK). There are simply two **possibilities**.

Now if we unify the two different formats into one, it still fits into the document, or the "old behaviors" pretty well -- the `$results` is still in one of the possible formats given...

Well, I am a newbie in software engineering. My understanding for BC might be wrong anyway.

UPDATE: Oops. I realized that for those who happened to see the second format in their apps and only dealt with the second format, the change might break their code however. My fault.

> UPDATE: Oops. I realized that for those who happened to see the second format in their apps and only dealt with the second format, the change might break their code however. My fault.

Spot on.

What about building a consistent output but only use it if you pass an extra option in the model's find method ? This provides backwards compatibility and giving developers the option to use the consistent output...

Something like:

```
$this->Model->find('first', array('afterFind' => 'consistent'));
```

For anyone dealing with this problem, here's a link to a hacky workaround:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14106283/cakephp-2-x-is-the-primary-flag-on-modelafterfind-actually-useful/16159420#16159420
